verdict:
# Adjudication — Keyloop, Principal Architect, Hyderabad (hybrid)

## TECHNICAL SCORE: 89.6 / 100

**Weights sum to exactly 1.00. Arithmetic, shown in full:**

| # | Criterion | Weight | /10 | weight x score | points lost |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Enterprise-scale architecture transformation | 0.14 | 9 | 1.26 | 1.40 |
| 2 | Multi-tenant SaaS platform architecture (named ownership area) | 0.18 | 10 | 1.80 | 0.00 |
| 3 | Cloud platforms, distributed systems, platform engineering | 0.15 | 9 | 1.35 | 1.50 |
| 4 | Observability, SRE, cost optimisation | 0.12 | 9 | 1.08 | 1.20 |
| 5 | Data architecture | 0.11 | 9 | 0.99 | 1.10 |
| 6 | Executive communication, influence without authority | 0.08 | 9 | 0.72 | 0.80 |
| 7 | AI-native platform strategy (agent orchestration, safety standards, bets) | 0.14 | 8 | 1.12 | **2.80** |
| 8 | Senior-IC scope: coaching, ROI, build/buy/adopt | 0.08 | 8 | 0.64 | 1.60 |
| | **TOTAL** | **1.00** | | **8.96** | **10.40** |

`sum(weight x score) = 8.96` -> `8.96 x 10 = 89.6`. Losses sum to 10.40, and `100 - 10.40 = 89.6`. Both routes agree.

**Every deduction on this rubric is a RAMP ITEM. There is no CAPABILITY CAP anywhere on it.** That is the headline: the posting names nothing he cannot do, and its two hardest lines — multi-tenancy as an owned standard, and the AI-native section — are the two threads his own record is deepest on. What holds the score under 95 is scope and scale, not capability: the largest estate he has transformed is ~300 enterprise customers, the AI strategy he set was for one ~20-engineer client engagement, the cloud is one cloud, and the LLM guardrails shipped in split form.

Above ModMed at 88.9 and Yes Madam at 88.375, and the highest technical score in the v2 workspace to date — but by tenths, and on a seat where the score's ceiling is honest, not tactical.

---

## THE BINDING CONSTRAINT: the AI-native section, at 2.80 points

Criterion 7 loses **2.80 points — 27% of everything this rubric loses** — and it is the posting's own self-declared differentiator ("the section that distinguishes this posting", jd.md). The loss has two parts and neither can be written away:

1. **The guardrails shipped in split form.** KQ1's field-level claim grammar is live; KQ9's shared contract is unsigned and its narrator ships off by default — `kq10-cross-domain.html` says it in its own diagram: *"Synthesize · per-patient chain narrative · strong tier · off by default"*. Card bullet 15's *"100% uncited claims rejected"* is a design property, not a production measurement. Any guardrail bullet must be worded shipped-where-live. That wording is the lift, and it costs nothing; a blanket "deployed LLM guardrails" claim is exactly the kind of internal inconsistency Keyloop says its AI screening looks for.
2. **Scope, and a number he does not have.** The Claude Code / Codex rollout across ~20 engineers has no measured outcome (professional-journey.md line 672, OPEN), and CLAUDE.md forbids asking him again. The org-wide AI-strategy dimension of the JD is one step larger than anything in the record. Nothing closes this except the seat itself.

The second-largest loss is criterion 8's **1.60 points** (coaching architects as peers, and written ROI analyses — both absent in shape, present in outcome), with criterion 3's single-cloud record just behind at 1.50, followed by the scale ramps on transformation (1.40), SRE tooling (1.20) and warehouse-scale analytics (1.10).

## THE SMALLEST HONEST LIFT

The rubric already credits evidence wherever it exists in his files, so **no résumé edit moves this score**. What the edit moves is whether a reader — human or Keyloop's screening model — sees the evidence the rubric saw. Rule 7 re-vectoring, in this order:

1. **Merge the four user-confirmed card bullets the master still lacks, per-claim, never as a block** — bullet 10 (Kubernetes, Terraform, Fargate at 70% Spot, cost down 25–30%, deploy under 10 minutes), bullet 11 (HIPAA framework across 10 production pipelines), bullet 12 (10 queries on 4 reusable archetypes) and bullet 14 (multi-tenant isolation — tenant-scoped traversal-source wrapper, parquet partition, runtime assertion). Those four are, line for line, the posting's ownership areas: multi-tenancy, regulatory compliance, reusable AI infrastructure, cost optimisation. Strip bullet 15's and 16's target figures and bullet 5's 500-to-100,000 wording on the way in.
2. **Re-vector the Deque block toward "architectural standards"** — the org-ID-on-every-table decision, the regulated-bank carve-out against one codebase, and Jenkins → GitHub Actions with ISO 27001 are standards he owned, in the JD's own vocabulary.
3. **Word the AI bullets in the posting's terms** — LangGraph runtime with Postgres checkpoints answers "agent orchestration"; four archetypes across ten queries answers "reusable AI infrastructure"; in-VPC self-hosted Llama 3.1 and the Elasticsearch-not-Neptune serving decision answer "concrete architectural bets"; claim grammar live on KQ1 answers "standards that enable rather than block" — and say KQ1, not "the platform".

None of the three adds a claim. All three are already in files he has confirmed.

## THE HONEST CEILING

**89.6 is the ceiling on the evidence we hold. 95 is not honestly reachable on this seat**, and the shortfall is not a defect in the record — it is the gap between a strong IC architect's history and a posting written for someone who has already set AI strategy company-wide, transformed a larger estate, and worked across more than one cloud. Two points could move with his confirmation, not ours: if he has in fact coached other architects as peers, or written the investment case behind any of the cost decisions (the Go rewrite, Fargate Spot, the Artirix replacement), criterion 8 goes to 9 and the total to 90.4. Nothing else moves without evidence that does not exist, and no wording change may manufacture it.

The open claims are untouched and not delegated: the graph neural network wording, the four Rocket metrics, the 70–80% consolidation, the 27 ms / P95 16 ms pairing and the 500-to-100,000 wording all stay exactly as they are on the résumé; they are prep items for a room, not rubric inputs.

## REAL-WORLD GATES — named separately, none scored
